title: TikTok as a Source of Education and Misinformation in Lichen Sclerosus
screen_reason: Descriptive cross-sectional content analysis of TikTok videos about vulvar lichen sclerosus. The abstract reports an explicit share of items judged to contain misinformation ('46% contained misinformation') out of a reviewed sample of 100 scraped videos, i.e. a CONTENT prevalence estimate with a denominator. Extraction is limited to what the abstract supports; no full text was available.

estimates.country: Not stated (TikTok videos tagged #lichensclerosus / 'lichen sclerosus'; no country restriction reported)
estimates.measure_type: % of TikTok lichen sclerosus videos that contained misinformation
estimates.denominator: A sample of 100 TikTok videos tagged #lichensclerosus or 'lichen sclerosus', identified with the Apify scraper, sorted by view count and reviewed by 2 independent reviewers (videos not discussing lichen sclerosus excluded; the final analysed count is not given in the abstract)
estimates.definition: Video judged by the reviewers, using a coding document plus PEMAT and DISCERN, to contain misinformation; the operational criterion for 'misinformation' is not given in the abstract
estimates.misinfo_def: No explicit definition in the abstract; misinformation is contrasted with 'evidence-based medicine' and 'nonevidence-based approaches'
estimates.n: 100 videos sampled (final analysed n not stated)
estimates.source_quote: Quality assessment revealed 61% of videos were understandable, 27% actionable, and 46% contained misinformation.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two independent reviewers using a coding document, the Patient Educational Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT) and the DISCERN instrument; interrater reliability measured with Fleiss' kappa and intraclass correlation coefficient, but no reliability values are reported in the abstract
estimates.moderator_quote: Using the third-party data scraping tool Apify, TikTok videos tagged with #lichensclerosus or "lichen sclerosus" were identified and sorted by view count. A sample of 100 videos was reviewed by 2 independent reviewers, excluding those not discussing lichen sclerosus.
estimates.notes: Abstract-only text. Denominator is all videos in the topical sample -> CONTENT. denom_selection=curated because the sample is the top-100 by view count within the hashtag corpus. breadth=misleading because the abstract gives no operational definition and the contrast class is 'nonevidence-based', which is broader than outright falsity. year left empty: the abstract text carries neither a data-collection date nor a publication year. Confidence medium because the exact analysed denominator (after excluding off-topic videos) is not stated, so 46% may be of slightly fewer than 100 videos.

estimates.measure_type: % of treatment-related TikTok lichen sclerosus videos that included nonevidence-based approaches
estimates.denominator: Treatment-related videos within the reviewed sample (treatment was the topic of 48% of videos; the count is not stated)
estimates.definition: Video included a nonevidence-based treatment approach (as opposed to evidence-based medicine), coded with a neutral or positive sentiment
estimates.misinfo_def: No explicit definition in the abstract; 'evidence-based medicine' vs 'nonevidence-based approaches'
estimates.n: Treatment-related videos (48% of the reviewed sample; exact count not stated)
estimates.source_quote: Evidence-based medicine was discussed in 71.7% of treatment-related videos, while 51.7% included nonevidence-based approaches, with a neutral or positive sentiment.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two independent reviewers coding against evidence-based medicine; reliability statistics not reported in the abstract
estimates.moderator_quote: Evidence-based medicine was discussed in 71.7% of treatment-related videos, while 51.7% included nonevidence-based approaches, with a neutral or positive sentiment.
estimates.notes: ADJUDICATOR: keep or drop. Flagged borderline because the measure is whether a video 'included' a nonevidence-based approach, not whether the video itself is false: a video could mention a nonevidence-based remedy critically. It is a guideline-discordance judgement (which the instructions treat as CONTENT), so it is recorded as a stricter/broader definition variant of the 46% row, but its denominator is a subset (treatment-related videos only) whose size is never stated. Not summed or combined with the 46% row.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) PEMAT understandability (61%) and actionability (27%) and the DISCERN scores are information-quality measures with no truth/falsity judgement, so no row (they are not misinformation prevalence). (2) Creator-type shares (patients 46%, health care professionals 30%) and topic shares (clinical disease 52%, treatment 48%) are sample-composition descriptives, not misinformation shares. (3) 'Videos by health care professionals had less misinformation and higher quality scores' and 'Commercially biased videos were more understandable but contained more misinformation' are stated as comparisons with no accompanying percentages in the abstract, so no subgroup rows can be extracted. (4) No data-collection dates, country, exact final denominator, or reliability coefficients are recoverable from the abstract; a full text would be needed. (5) No exposure, sharing, recall or concentration measure is reported.

rob.design: Descriptive cross-sectional content analysis. Frame: TikTok videos tagged #lichensclerosus or 'lichen sclerosus', scraped with Apify and sorted by view count; the top 100 were reviewed, excluding videos not discussing lichen sclerosus. Two independent reviewers used a coding document plus PEMAT and DISCERN. Interrater reliability measured (Fleiss' kappa, ICC) but no values reported in the abstract. Analyses: t tests, Wilcoxon rank sum with Holm-Bonferroni. No response rate applicable. Country, dates and final analysed n are not reported in the available text.
rob.item6_quote: Videos were assessed using a coding document, the Patient Educational Materials Assessment Tool, and the DISCERN instrument.
rob.item10_quote: A sample of 100 videos was reviewed by 2 independent reviewers, excluding those not discussing lichen sclerosus. ... Quality assessment revealed 61% of videos were understandable, 27% actionable, and 46% contained misinformation.
